title: The Amber Loom
author: Barış Kısır
premise: In a village where the weaving of cloth is believed to weave the seasons themselves, apprentice weaver Ilsa finds a loom threaded with amber — the locked color of a village winter that should have ended three years ago. To un-weave it she must follow the thread to the woman who wove it, her own grandmother, buried in the hill.
short_description: Apprentice weaver Ilsa inherits a loom threaded with the locked amber of a winter that should have ended — and must follow the thread into the hill to un-weave it.
long_description: In Brekkelund, the seasons are threads, and each year the weavers of the Hall weave Spring over Winter. Three years ago Ilsa's grandmother Anke wove the season that refused — an amber thread that locked the village into cold, famine, and the grey people, villagers half-unwoven into thread themselves. Now the loom sits threaded with amber, warm and alive, and apprentice weaver Ilsa discovers her grandmother wove herself into the pattern to hold the winter — because something older than the seasons wants the village's cold: the Hill-God, owed a debt in wool. To un-weave the winter without unmaking the village, Ilsa must enter the weave itself, confront the Hill-God in the underhill loom-chamber, and re-weave the amber as something the debt has never seen: dusk.
main_characters: Ilsa Wren — apprentice weaver, nineteen, inventive and afraid
Greta — the village weaver, keeper of secrets, missing a hand lost to the loom
Anke — Ilsa's grandmother, present in the weave
Tobin — shepherd boy, Ilsa's friend, woven grey
The Hill-God — the debt in wool, speaks in loom creaks
The Elders — guardians of the Hall
